correctness.rationale: For 0<a,b<1/M and fixed-by-iterate points in the smooth two-sided core, the central derivative is M^(number beta-number alpha), so a neutral return has 2m symbols. Rotating each balanced binary bridge to its minimum produces nested Dyck brackets. Matched labels are necessary and sufficient for identity central return and give M^m choices; the original-cut interval is an M-adic cylinder of length M^{-j}, j=-minimum prefix height. Expanding base and contracting stable coordinates have unique strict-interior fixed coordinates; mismatched affine center return cannot have any fixed point. A reflection-principle bridge count yields the exact histogram, summing disjoint line lengths gives Hausdorff measure. Bounded domination and Stirling prove m^-3/2 coefficient; a telescoping binomial CDF and length weighting prove the two depth laws. Exact fraction-based enumeration checks M=2,3, m=1,2,3 without purporting to prove infinite cases.

originality.rationale: The established symbolic count M^m binomial(2m,m), Dyck coding and existence of neutral periodic intervals are explicitly prior work. The proposed statement supplies a different geometric invariant: the exact partition of interval lengths by excursion minimum, its sharp Hausdorff 1-measure coefficient, and two inequivalent natural sampling laws. Primary full-text implication comparisons found no geometric histogram or stronger statement entailing it; this is a bounded same-model priority assessment, not proof of absolute novelty.

value.rationale: Neutral nonhyperbolic periodic continua are explicitly excluded from the motivating equidistribution theorems although their symbolic totals are known, making their geometric size a natural unresolved observable. The depth-to-length law uncovers an exact complete histogram, a physical Hausdorff measure with a non-obvious m^-3/2 prefactor, and a meaningful sharp distinction between uniform component sampling and physical-length-biased sampling. It is not a routine restatement of the pre-existing unweighted periodic count; the difference matters for typical geometric behavior.
